\section{Overview}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{FABL.Chapter03.GoldreichLevin.Controller}.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Restricted Fourier weight estimates]
\lean{FABL.RestrictedFourierWeightEstimate}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p084-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p084-b003
}
\label{FABL.RestrictedFourierWeightEstimate}
\leanok
For a natural number $n$, a restricted Fourier weight estimate assigns a rational number
to each pair consisting of a set of coordinates $J\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ and a
subset of $J$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Accuracy of a restricted Fourier weight estimate]
\lean{FABL.IsAccurateRestrictedFourierWeightEstimate}
\label{FABL.IsAccurateRestrictedFourierWeightEstimate}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.GoldreichLevinThreshold, FABL.RestrictedFourierWeightEstimate, FABL.restrictedFourierWeight}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f$ be a Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional cube,
let $\tau$ be a rational number with $0<\tau\leq1$, and let $W$ assign a rational number
$W(J,S)$ to every subset $J$ of the coordinates and every subset $S\subseteq J$. The
estimate is accurate if, for every such $J$ and $S$, its error in estimating the
restricted Fourier weight of $f$ on $J$ at $S$ is less than $\tau^2/4$; that is,
$|W(J,S)-\widehat W_f(J,S)|<\tau^2/4$, where $\widehat W_f(J,S)$ denotes that restricted
Fourier weight.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Goldreich–Levin children]
\lean{FABL.goldreichLevinChildren}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p085-b004}
\label{FABL.goldreichLevinChildren}
\leanok
For a natural number $n$, a coordinate $i\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, and a set of coordinates
$S\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, the children of $S$ at $i$ are the family consisting of
$S$ and $S\cup\{i\}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Goldreich–Levin candidates]
\lean{FABL.goldreichLevinCandidates}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p084-b006,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p085-b001
}
\label{FABL.goldreichLevinCandidates}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.goldreichLevinChildren}
For a natural number $n$, a coordinate $i\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, and a finite family
$\mathcal A$ of sets of coordinates, the candidate family is the union, over
$S\in\mathcal A$, of the two children $S$ and $S\cup\{i\}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Goldreich–Levin candidate membership]
\lean{FABL.mem_goldreichLevinCandidates_iff}
\label{FABL.mem_goldreichLevinCandidates_iff}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.goldreichLevinCandidates, FABL.goldreichLevinChildren}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $i$ be a coordinate in $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, and let
$A$ be a finite family of subsets of the coordinates. A set $T$ belongs to the family
formed by taking, for each $S\in A$, the sets $S$ and $S\cup\{i\}$ if and only if
there is some $S\in A$ such that $T=S$ or $T=S\cup\{i\}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Candidate sets extend the coordinate prefix]
\lean{FABL.goldreichLevinCandidates_subset_prefixCoordinates_succ}
\label{FABL.goldreichLevinCandidates_subset_prefixCoordinates_succ}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.goldreichLevinCandidates, FABL.mem_goldreichLevinCandidates_iff, FABL.prefixCoordinates, FABL.prefixCoordinates_succ}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number and let $k<n$. Suppose an active family consists of subsets
of the first $k$ coordinates of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$. For each active set $S$, form the two
candidates $S$ and $S\cup\{k+1\}$. Every set in the resulting family is contained in the
first $k+1$ coordinates.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Retained Goldreich–Levin candidates]
\lean{FABL.goldreichLevinRetained}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p085-b001,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p085-b002
}
\label{FABL.goldreichLevinRetained}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.GoldreichLevinThreshold, FABL.RestrictedFourierWeightEstimate, FABL.freeFrequencyPart, FABL.goldreichLevinCandidates, FABL.prefixCoordinates}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $0<\tau\le 1$, let $E$ be a restricted Fourier weight
estimate, and let $k<n$ be a natural number. Given a finite active family $\mathcal A$
of sets of coordinates, form the candidates at coordinate $k$ and retain precisely those
sets $S$ for which $\tau^2/2<E(J,S\cap J)$, where $J=\{0,\ldots,k\}$ and $E(J,\cdot)$
denotes the estimate on subsets of $J$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Goldreich–Levin refinement step]
\lean{FABL.goldreichLevinRefine}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p085-b001,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p085-b004
}
\label{FABL.goldreichLevinRefine}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.GoldreichLevinThreshold, FABL.RestrictedFourierWeightEstimate, FABL.goldreichLevinActiveCap, FABL.goldreichLevinRetained}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $0<\tau\le 1$, let $E$ be a restricted Fourier weight
estimate, and let $k<n$ be a natural number. For a finite active family $\mathcal A$,
compute the retained candidates at coordinate $k$; return that family if its cardinality
is at most $\lceil 4/\tau^2\rceil$, and otherwise return no value.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Goldreich–Levin iteration through a prefix]
\lean{FABL.goldreichLevinRunUpTo}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p084-b006,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p085-b001,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p085-b004
}
\label{FABL.goldreichLevinRunUpTo}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.GoldreichLevinThreshold, FABL.RestrictedFourierWeightEstimate, FABL.goldreichLevinRefine}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $0<\tau\le 1$, and let $E$ be a restricted Fourier
weight estimate. For each natural number $k\le n$, define an optional finite family
recursively: at $k=0$ it is the singleton family containing the empty set; at $k+1$, if
the value at $k$ is absent, the value is absent, and otherwise apply the refinement step
at coordinate $k$ to that family.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Goldreich–Levin output]
\lean{FABL.goldreichLevinOutput}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p085-b001,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p089-b010,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p091-b002
}
\label{FABL.goldreichLevinOutput}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.GoldreichLevinThreshold, FABL.RestrictedFourierWeightEstimate, FABL.goldreichLevinRunUpTo}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $0<\tau\le 1$, and let $E$ be a restricted Fourier
weight estimate. The output is the optional finite family obtained by running the
Goldreich–Levin iteration through stage $n$.
\end{definition}

  {FABL.goldreichLevinRetained}
  {context}
  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p085-b001,
    pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p085-b002}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $0<\tau\leq 1$ be rational, let an estimate assign a
rational number to every finite coordinate set $J\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ and every
finite subset of $J$, and let the estimate differ from the true restricted Fourier
weight of a Boolean target function by less than $\tau^2/4$ at every such pair. Let
$k<n$, let $A$ be a finite family of subsets of the coordinates, and let $S$ belong to
the retained family obtained from the candidates $U$ and $U\cup\{k\}$ for $U\in A$ by
keeping those whose estimate on the first $k+1$ coordinates, restricted to their part in
that prefix, exceeds $\tau^2/2$. Then the true restricted Fourier weight on that prefix
at the free part of $S$ is strictly greater than $\tau^2/4$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Successor prefix candidate membership]
\lean{FABL.prefixFrequency_succ_mem_goldreichLevinCandidates}
\label{FABL.prefixFrequency_succ_mem_goldreichLevinCandidates}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.goldreichLevinCandidates, FABL.mem_goldreichLevinCandidates_iff, FABL.prefixFrequency, FABL.prefixFrequency_succ}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $k<n$, let $U$ be a subset of $\in n$, and let $A$ be a
family of subsets of $\in n$. For each natural number $r$, write $P_r=\{i\in U:i<r\}$,
and for a subset $S$ of $\in n$, its children at index $k$ are $S$ and $S\cup\{k\}$. If
$P_k\in A$, then $P_{k+1}$ is among the children at index $k$ of some member of $A$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Prefix support of retained frequencies]
\lean{FABL.goldreichLevinRunUpTo_prefixes}
\label{FABL.goldreichLevinRunUpTo_prefixes}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.GoldreichLevinThreshold, FABL.RestrictedFourierWeightEstimate, FABL.goldreichLevinActiveCap, FABL.goldreichLevinCandidates_subset_prefixCoordinates_succ, FABL.goldreichLevinRetained, FABL.goldreichLevinRunUpTo, FABL.prefixCoordinates}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $0<\tau\le1$, and let an estimate assign a rational
number to every coordinate set and every frequency subset of that set. For every $k\le
n$, if the run through stage $k$ returns an active family $A$, then every $S\in A$ is
contained in the first $k$ coordinates, namely $\{i\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}:i<k\}$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\tau$ be rational with $0<\tau\le 1$, and let an
estimate assign a rational number to each pair consisting of a coordinate set $J$ and a
subset of $J$. Suppose $k+1\le n$, and suppose the run through step $k+1$ returns the
family $A$. Then every $S\in A$ belongs to the retained family at step $k$ for some
preceding active family.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{5}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$, and let $0<\tau\le1$.
Suppose rational estimates of the restricted Fourier weights of $f$ are within
$\tau^2/4$ of their true values for every coordinate set and every subset of that set.
If the Goldreich–Levin procedure with threshold $\tau$ returns a family $A$ of
coordinate sets, then every $U\in A$ has Fourier coefficient satisfying
$\tau/2<|\widehat f(U)|$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Existence of the Goldreich–Levin output]
\lean{FABL.goldreichLevinOutput_exists_of_accurate}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p085-b001,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p085-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p083-b002
}
\label{FABL.goldreichLevinOutput_exists_of_accurate}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.GoldreichLevinThreshold, FABL.IsAccurateRestrictedFourierWeightEstimate, FABL.RestrictedFourierWeightEstimate, FABL.goldreichLevinOutput, FABL.goldreichLevinRunUpTo_exists_of_accurate}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ be a Boolean function,
and let $\tau\in\mathbb{Q}$ satisfy $0<\tau\le 1$. For each coordinate set
$J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ and each $S\subseteq J$, suppose a rational estimate differs
by less than $\tau^2/4$ from the sum of squared Fourier coefficients of $f$ over all
sets of the form $S\cup T$, where $T\subseteq J^c$. Then the Goldreich–Levin procedure
with threshold $\tau$ and these estimates returns a finite family of coordinate sets.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Cardinality bound for the Goldreich–Levin output]
\lean{FABL.goldreichLevinOutput_card_le}
\statementsource{HILL99}{pdf-130039751e9f-p018-b006}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p083-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p085-b003
}
\label{FABL.goldreichLevinOutput_card_le}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.GoldreichLevinThreshold, FABL.IsAccurateRestrictedFourierWeightEstimate, FABL.RestrictedFourierWeightEstimate, FABL.fourierCoeff, FABL.goldreichLevinOutput, FABL.goldreichLevinOutput_sound_of_accurate, FABL.sum_sq_fourierCoeff_eq_one}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f:\{−1,1\}^n\to\{−1,1\}$ be any target function, let
$0<\tau\le1$ be a rational threshold, and let an estimate assign a rational number to
each pair consisting of a coordinate subset $J$ and a subset $S\subseteq J$. Suppose
each estimate differs from the corresponding restricted Fourier weight of $f$ by less
than $\tau^2/4$. If the Goldreich–Levin output for this estimate is a family $A$, then
its cardinality satisfies $|A|\le4/\tau^2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Goldreich–Levin candidate bound]
\lean{FABL.card_goldreichLevinCandidates_le_two_mul}
\label{FABL.card_goldreichLevinCandidates_le_two_mul}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.goldreichLevinCandidates, FABL.goldreichLevinChildren}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $i$ be a coordinate among the first $n$ coordinates,
and let $A$ be a finite family of subsets of those coordinates. Form the candidate
family by taking, for each $S\in A$, the two sets $S$ and $S\cup\{i\}$. Its cardinality
is at most $2|A|$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Accuracy at a Goldreich–Levin stage]
\lean{FABL.IsAccurateGoldreichLevinStage}
\label{FABL.IsAccurateGoldreichLevinStage}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.GoldreichLevinThreshold, FABL.RestrictedFourierWeightEstimate, FABL.freeFrequencyPart, FABL.goldreichLevinCandidates, FABL.prefixCoordinates, FABL.restrictedFourierWeight}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f$ be a Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional cube,
let $\tau$ be rational with $0<\tau\leq1$, and let $W(J,S)$ be a rational estimate for
each coordinate subset $J$ and each $S\subseteq J$. Choose $k<n$ and a family $A$ of
subsets of the coordinates. Put $J=\{0,\ldots,k\}$. The estimate is accurate at stage
$k$ for $A$ if, for every Goldreich–Levin candidate $S$ formed from coordinate $k$ and
the active family $A$, its error $|W(J,S')-\widehat W_f(J,S')|$ on the restricted
Fourier weight is less than $\tau^2/4$, where $S'$ is the candidate's free-frequency
part within $J$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Accuracy of a Goldreich–Levin stage]
\lean{FABL.isAccurateGoldreichLevinStage_of_isAccurateRestrictedFourierWeightEstimate}
\label{FABL.isAccurateGoldreichLevinStage_of_isAccurateRestrictedFourierWeightEstimate}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.GoldreichLevinThreshold, FABL.IsAccurateGoldreichLevinStage, FABL.IsAccurateRestrictedFourierWeightEstimate, FABL.RestrictedFourierWeightEstimate, FABL.freeFrequencyPart, FABL.prefixCoordinates}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f$ be a Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign
cube, let $0<\tau\le 1$, and let $E$ assign a rational estimate to each coordinate set
$J\subseteq[n]$ and each subset of $J$. Suppose that for every such $J$ and subset $S$,
the estimate differs from the restricted Fourier weight of $f$ by less than $\tau^2/4$.
For any $k<n$ and any family of subsets of $[n]$, consider the candidates obtained by
adjoining or omitting coordinate $k$ from members of that family; for every candidate
$S$, the estimate at the prefix of the first $k+1$ coordinates and the free-coordinate
part of $S$ differs from the corresponding restricted Fourier weight by less than
$\tau^2/4$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $0<\tau\leq 1$ be rational, let an estimate assign
rational values to finite coordinate sets and their subsets, and let $k<n$ and $A$ be a
finite family of coordinate subsets. Suppose the estimate differs from the true
restricted Fourier weight by less than $\tau^2/4$ for every candidate generated from $A$
by either leaving a set unchanged or adjoining coordinate $k$, using the candidate's
part in the first $k+1$ coordinates. If $S$ is retained among those candidates by having
estimated weight greater than $\tau^2/2$ on that prefix, then its true restricted
Fourier weight, evaluated at its part in the prefix, is strictly greater than
$\tau^2/4$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Goldreich–Levin active-set invariant]
\lean{FABL.GoldreichLevinActiveInvariant}
\label{FABL.GoldreichLevinActiveInvariant}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.GoldreichLevinThreshold, FABL.fourierCoeff, FABL.freeFrequencyPart, FABL.prefixCoordinates, FABL.prefixFrequency, FABL.restrictedFourierWeight}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{\pm1\}$ be a Boolean function, let
$\tau$ be a rational number with $0<\tau\le 1$, let $k\in\mathbb N$, and let $A$ be a
family of subsets of $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$. The invariant requires that every $S\in A$ be
contained in the first $k$ coordinates; that every set of coordinates $U$ whose Fourier
coefficient for $f$ has absolute value at least $\tau$ has its prefix-frequency part at
level $k$ in $A$; and, for every $k>0$ and every $S\in A$, the restricted Fourier weight
of $f$ on the free-frequency part associated with $S$ and the first $k$ coordinates is
strictly greater than $\tau^2/4$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Initial active invariant]
\lean{FABL.goldreichLevinActiveInvariant_zero}
\label{FABL.goldreichLevinActiveInvariant_zero}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.GoldreichLevinActiveInvariant, FABL.GoldreichLevinThreshold}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$, and let $\tau$ be rational
with $0<\tau\le 1$. At stage zero, the singleton family consisting of the empty
frequency set satisfies the active invariant.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Preservation of the active invariant]
\lean{FABL.goldreichLevinActiveInvariant_retained}
\label{FABL.goldreichLevinActiveInvariant_retained}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.GoldreichLevinActiveInvariant, FABL.GoldreichLevinThreshold, FABL.IsAccurateGoldreichLevinStage, FABL.RestrictedFourierWeightEstimate, FABL.goldreichLevinCandidates_subset_prefixCoordinates_succ, FABL.goldreichLevinRetained, FABL.heavy_prefix_mem_goldreichLevinRetained_of_stageAccurate, FABL.restrictedFourierWeight_gt_quarter_of_mem_goldreichLevinRetained_of_stageAccurate}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$, let $\tau$ be rational with
$0<\tau\le 1$, and let $E$ assign a rational estimate to each restricted Fourier weight.
Let $k<n$ and let $\mathcal A$ be a finite family of frequency sets. If $\mathcal A$
satisfies the active invariant at stage $k$, and every candidate at stage $k$ has
estimated restricted Fourier weight within $\tau^2/4$ of its true restricted Fourier
weight, then the family retained by the stated candidate and threshold rule satisfies
the active invariant at stage $k+1$.
\end{theorem}

  {FABL.goldreichLevinActiveInvariant_retained}
  {context}
  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p085-b001,
    pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p085-b002,
    pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p085-b004}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f:\{\pm1\}^n\to\{\pm1\}$, let $\tau\in\mathbb{Q}$
satisfy $0<\tau\le1$, let $E$ assign a rational estimate to each restricted Fourier
weight, and let $k<n$ be a natural number. Let $A$ be a finite family of subsets of the
first $n$ coordinates. Assume that every set in $A$ is contained in the first $k$
coordinates; that for every frequency set $U$, if $\tau\le|\widehat f(U)|$, then the
part of $U$ among the first $k$ coordinates belongs to $A$; and that, when $k>0$, every
$S\in A$ has restricted Fourier weight greater than $\tau^2/4$ on the first $k$
coordinates. Also assume that on every candidate formed from $A$ by either keeping a set
or adjoining coordinate $k$, the estimate for its part among the first $k+1$ coordinates
differs from the corresponding restricted Fourier weight by less than $\tau^2/4$. Then
the number of such candidates whose estimated weight is greater than $\tau^2/2$ is at
most $\lceil4/\tau^2\rceil$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Goldreich levin refine eq some retained of stage accurate]
\lean{FABL.goldreichLevinRefine_eq_some_retained_of_stageAccurate}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p085-b001,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p085-b002
